stories.headline: Democrats win House and Senate in midterm rout, flipping seven Senate seats including Texas

key_facts.fact: NBC News projects Democrats will take control of both the House and the Senate in January, in what it calls a repudiation of President Trump's agenda.
key_facts.excerpt: Democrats will take control of the House and the Senate in January, NBC News projects, winning seats in deep red and battleground states in a repudiation of President Donald Trump's agenda.

key_facts.fact: Democrats flipped seven Senate seats: Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Democrats flipped seven seats in the upper chamber, including Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas.

key_facts.fact: US media projected a 54-44 Democratic Senate as of 09:45 GMT Wednesday; Republicans previously held the Senate 53-47 and the House 219-215.
key_facts.excerpt: where the party previously held a 53-47 advantage in the Senate and a 219-215 majority in the House of Representatives. US media projected a 54-44 Democratic majority in the Senate as of 0945GMT Wednesday

key_facts.fact: An NBC News analysis estimates Democrats will win at least 258 House seats, against the 218 needed for a majority; the estimate could still move by a few seats.
key_facts.excerpt: Democrats will win at least 258 House seats, an estimate that could still tick up or down by a few seats but will be well beyond the 218 needed to secure a majority, an NBC News analysis shows.

key_facts.fact: Democrats flipped governorships in Texas, Georgia, Nevada, Ohio and Iowa.
key_facts.excerpt: In gubernatorial races, Democrats flipped Texas, Georgia, Nevada, Ohio and Iowa.

key_facts.fact: NBC News exit polls put Trump's disapproval at 62%, and nearly half of voters said they saw the election as an opportunity to rebuke him.
key_facts.excerpt: NBC News Exit Polls showed a dissatisfied electorate, with Trump's disapproval rating at 62%... Nearly half of voters said they viewed the election as an opportunity to rebuke Trump.

key_facts.fact: Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers in Michigan to become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate; in Kansas, Adam Hamilton won a seat Republicans had held since 1932.
key_facts.excerpt: In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate... In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton won a Senate seat held by Republicans since 1932.

key_facts.fact: Control of the chambers lets Democrats run congressional committees, open investigations of the Trump administration and block Republican legislation when the new Congress convenes in January 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The Democratic takeover will allow the party to control congressional committees, launch investigations into the Trump administration and block Republican legislative initiatives when the new Congress convenes in January 2027.

stories.headline: Voters in at least 29 US jurisdictions pass data center bans or limits on midterm ballots

key_facts.fact: Voters in at least 29 US jurisdictions passed bans or restrictions on data centers on Tuesday, according to The Washington Post.
key_facts.excerpt: Voters in at least 29 jurisdictions across the country passed bans or restrictions on data centers Tuesday, reflecting the widespread public revulsion to the facilities

key_facts.fact: S&P counted more than 145 US data center projects delayed or canceled through early August.
key_facts.excerpt: S&P says 145+ US projects were delayed or canceled through early August (Techmeme summary of the Post's report)

key_facts.fact: In an NBC exit poll cited by the FT, 56% of voters said AI and data centers were a crucial or major factor in their votes for Congress.
key_facts.excerpt: NBC exit poll: 56% said AI and data centers had been a 'crucial or a major factor' in their Congress votes, as Democratic candidates pledged to halt development (Techmeme summary of the FT's report)

key_facts.fact: Ohio held 21 of the 41 data center ballot measures nationwide, across 18 municipalities, and at least 14 municipalities passed bans or other restrictions; the state already had 125 local moratoriums.
key_facts.excerpt: Ohio residents across 18 municipalities voted on 21 ballot measures on data centers on Tuesday, more than half of the 41 data center-related ballot measures across the country... at least 14 municipalities passing bans or other restrictions

key_facts.fact: Trenton, Ohio passed a ban 80% to 20%, which organizers hope will keep out an 18-building AWS data center; Ashville voted to block a campus already under construction.
key_facts.excerpt: In Trenton, a ban passed 80% to 20%. Organizers hope it will keep an 18-building Amazon Web Services data center out of the city... Ashville residents voted in favor of entirely blocking a data center campus that is already under construction.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reports that Democratic gubernatorial wins from Texas and Georgia to Ohio and Pennsylvania will expose 50% of AI data center proposals to more scrutiny and pushback.
key_facts.excerpt: Democratic gubernatorial wins from Texas and Georgia to Ohio and Pennsylvania are set to expose 50% of AI data center proposals to more scrutiny and pushback (Techmeme summary)

key_facts.fact: Politico reports the industry's biggest donors poured hundreds of millions of dollars over the cycle into boosting pro-industry Republicans, and that Democrats turned frustration with tech into a midterm advantage.
key_facts.excerpt: The blue wave carried a repudiation of Silicon Valley's biggest donors who over the cycle poured hundreds of millions of dollars to boost pro-industry Republicans

stories.headline: Trump says Iran strikes aren't imminent, admits war cost votes; IRGC claims four tankers hit mines

key_facts.fact: Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday evening he had no immediate plans to order new strikes on Iran, saying 'we're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it.'
key_facts.excerpt: President Trump told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday evening that he had no immediate plans to order new strikes on Iran... 'we're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it.'

key_facts.fact: Trump acknowledged the war was partly to blame for the Republican losses but told The Wall Street Journal he did not regret it and 'would have done it again.'
key_facts.excerpt: President Trump acknowledged Tuesday night that the war with Iran was partially to blame for the GOP's resounding midterm elections losses. But Mr. Trump told The Wall Street Journal he didn't regret the conflict and added he 'would have done it again.'

key_facts.fact: The IRGC claimed on Wednesday that four oil tankers were destroyed after striking naval mines in a prohibited lane south of the Strait of Hormuz and that two other vessels were detained; Al Jazeera notes the claim could not be independently linked to a separate UKMTO report.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC claimed on Wednesday that four oil tankers were destroyed after striking naval mines while attempting to pass through a prohibited shipping lane south of the Strait of Hormuz... It could not be independently verified whether the incidents reported by UKMTO and the IRGC were linked.

key_facts.fact: UKMTO reported two projectiles struck a tanker's engine room about 14 nautical miles northeast of Limah, Oman, on Tuesday, with no casualties.
key_facts.excerpt: UKMTO reported that two unidentified projectiles struck a tanker's engine room about 14 nautical miles (26km) northeast of Oman's coastal village of Limah on Tuesday. No casualties were reported.

key_facts.fact: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called the US response to Tehran's seven conditions 'not convincing' and said Hormuz reopens only if they are met; Qatar said both sides remain committed to talks.
key_facts.excerpt: 'America's response to Iran's rights and demands was not convincing, and they must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them,' he wrote on X. 'Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.'

key_facts.fact: A statement attributed to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said anyone expecting a shift in US policy after the midterms was 'seriously mistaken' and warned that if attacks recur 'the war's scope will become much wider.'
key_facts.excerpt: said anyone expecting a shift in U.S. policy regarding the war with Iran in the wake of the American midterm elections was 'seriously mistaken.'... 'should such aggressions be repeated, the war's scope will become much wider.'

key_facts.fact: Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the election results showed Americans rejected the war and warned of 'a Nightmare' if Trump does not heed them.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's chief negotiator said Wednesday that the U.S. midterm election results reflected Americans' rejection of the war... Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf added a warning that if Mr. Trump does not heed the message from American voters, it will bring 'a Nightmare.'

key_facts.fact: The Hormuz standoff has kept global oil prices 60% to 70% above pre-war levels, according to CBS News.
key_facts.excerpt: the standoff has seen the Islamic Republic continue threatening and attacking commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, which in turn has kept global oil prices 60% to 70% higher than they were before the war started

stories.headline: Democratic sweep lifts gold 3% past $4,000, hits dollar and defense stocks; US futures erase losses

key_facts.fact: US stock futures fell as much as 2% overnight, then reversed to rally around 1%; MSCI's All-World index was up 0.3% and Europe's STOXX 600 up 1.4% to two-month highs.
key_facts.excerpt: MSCI's All-World index was up 0.3%, while Europe's STOXX 600... jumped 1.4% to two-month highs. US stock futures also reversed course to rally around 1%, having fallen by as much as 2% overnight.

key_facts.fact: Spot gold rose 3% to $4,047.57 an ounce, and the US dollar index slid 0.5% to 101.32, its lowest in over a month.
key_facts.excerpt: Gold futures jumped 2.9% to $4,055.40 an ounce, while the spot price soared 3% to $4,047.57... slid 0.5% to its lowest point in over a month to 101.32.

key_facts.fact: Spot silver jumped 4.27% to $51.90 per ounce, platinum rose 3.38% and palladium 5.57%.
key_facts.excerpt: spot silver jumped 4.27% to trade at $51.90 per ounce... platinum, which jumped 3.38% to trade at $1,463.95, and palladium, which was 5.57% higher at $985.50

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.92%; Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid says investors now price around 50 basis points of Fed rate rises until 2027, below the pre-election level.
key_facts.excerpt: the rate on the benchmark 10-year government bond declining to 4.92%... investors also now pricing in around 50 basis points of rate rises from the Federal Reserve until 2027, below the pre-election level.

key_facts.fact: Defense stocks fell on both sides of the Atlantic: BAE Systems nearly 4%, Rheinmetall 2%, and Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman and RTX 1.5% to 2.8%.
key_facts.excerpt: defence stocks on both sides of the Atlantic fell, with Britain's BAE Systems down nearly 4%, Germany's Rheinmetall down 2% and US weapons makers Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman and RTX down 1.5% to 2.8%.

key_facts.fact: Clean energy names rallied: Ørsted rose about 7.4%, Nordex 6.5% and Vestas about 5%, while European bank stocks gained 2.8%.
key_facts.excerpt: Bank stocks leapt 2.8%... Denmark's Vestas Wind Systems jumped about 5% and Ørsted surged 7.4% while the German wind turbine company Nordex leapt 6.5%.

key_facts.fact: Assets sensitive to US foreign policy gained: Ukraine's international bonds hit their highest since September and the dollar fell nearly 1% against the Mexican peso; Brent was at $103.17, down 0.4%.
key_facts.excerpt: The Mexican peso strengthened, leaving the dollar down nearly 1%... The price of Ukraine's international bonds hit its highest since September... Brent crude was down 0.4% on the day at $103.17 a barrel.

stories.headline: Binance says North Korea used fake LinkedIn interviews and a rigged Homebrew ad in its $6.3B hack

key_facts.fact: Binance disclosed on Tuesday that North Korean hackers carried out last week's $6.3B theft, which Fortune calls the biggest in crypto history, using social engineering and malicious software.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance on Tuesday disclosed that North Korean hackers used a mix of social engineering and malicious software to pull off last week's $6.3 billion heist, the biggest in crypto history.

key_facts.fact: Hackers targeted an engineer on LinkedIn and ran fake interviews, including one with a supposed CEO of a fictitious company, to get him to download an 'assignment' that let them into Binance's systems.
key_facts.excerpt: the hackers targeted a Binance engineer on LinkedIn and arranged a series of fake job interviews in order to persuade the employee to download an 'assignment' that let them invade the company's systems.

key_facts.fact: A separate ad campaign tricked another engineer into downloading a tampered version of Homebrew; Binance detected and removed it, but not before the hackers learned about the staff who managed its wallets.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance says it detected the fake Homebrew download and removed it from the employee's machine, but not before the hackers discovered critical information about the engineer's role and others who managed the company's wallets.

key_facts.fact: After taking over one engineer's laptop, the attackers used Binance's own internal AI tool to compromise other accounts, though Fortune says the attack relied primarily on conventional phishing.
key_facts.excerpt: The attacker leveraged the compromised computer of Engineer B and used an internal AI tool to gain control over the Wallet DevOps Engineer A and another Wallet Software Engineer C.

key_facts.fact: Binance recovered about $2.5B after Tether and Circle froze stolen stablecoins, and says it has replenished 98% of the stolen coins from reserves and other sources.
key_facts.excerpt: it was able to recover around $2.5 billion of that after two companies, Tether and Circle, moved to freeze stolen stablecoins... it has replenished 98% of the stolen coins from reserve funds and other sources.

key_facts.fact: Binance says it detected and prevented 57 North Korea-related hacking attempts in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: in 2026, it had detected and prevented 57 North Korea-related hacking attempts.

stories.headline: Canva restructuring hits 1,271 jobs, 22% of staff, as growth slows; CEO calls it 'hardest moment'

key_facts.fact: Canva's restructure affects 1,271 jobs, or 22% of its workforce, with some staff losing their roles and others asked to relocate to centralized hubs.
key_facts.excerpt: The shake-up will affect 1271 jobs, or 22 per cent of its workforce, with some staff to lose their roles and others asked to relocate to centralised hubs.

key_facts.fact: CEO Melanie Perkins told staff on Wednesday the company must 'refound Canva' after growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade, calling it 'the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history.'
key_facts.excerpt: told staff on Wednesday the Sydney design software maker needed to 'refound Canva' and return to small, empowered teams after its growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade.

key_facts.fact: Perkins did not directly link the cuts to AI, though she wrote that new technology was transforming what people create and expect from products.
key_facts.excerpt: Perkins did not directly link the cuts to the rise of artificial intelligence, though she wrote that new technology was transforming what people create and what they expect from the products they use.

key_facts.fact: Canva will merge its product, growth and platform teams into one product organization, cut management layers, and expect hybrid staff in the office two to three days a week from January.
key_facts.excerpt: Canva will merge its product, growth and platform teams into a single product organisation and cut management layers... hybrid staff will be expected in the office two to three days a week from January.

key_facts.fact: Canva cut its own valuation to $31B and its 2026 revenue growth forecast by a third to 20%, after sales grew 38% in 2025 and 45% the year before.
key_facts.excerpt: Canva itself slashed its own valuation of its business to $US31 billion as it downgraded its revenue forecast by a third to just 20 per cent this year. Sales grew 38 per cent in 2025 and 45 per cent the year before.

key_facts.fact: Canva delayed its biggest AI-led update because the cost of running AI for its more than 200 million free users was eating into profits.
key_facts.excerpt: It also delayed the rollout of its biggest AI-led software update because the cost of running AI for its more than 200 million free users was eating into its profits.
